question.text:
Let f(x) = x|x|. What is the highest order of derivative of f that exists at zero?
(A) No first derivative exists.
(B) First order only
(C) Second order only
(D) Third order only
(E) Derivatives of all orders exist.

solution.text:
′ ′
The first difference quotient is |h| → 0, so f (0) = 0. Away from zero, f (x) = 2|x|. The
next difference quotient is 2|h|/h, with one-sided limits −2 and 2, so the second derivative
fails. Existing lower derivatives do not guarantee higher ones.

solution.text:
Derivatives repeat every four orders. Since 101 ≡ 1 (mod 4), this derivative is cos x, whose
value at π/3 is 1/2.
